tests_without_counterpart: ctest:snappy_unittest: only runs a GoogleTest binary, whose cases are mapped one by one

gtest:Snappy.FindMatchLength: Tests snappy::internal::FindMatchLength, a C++ helper of snappy-internal.h with word-at-a-time code paths. The Rust compressor has a private prefix comparison with no public API and no such paths; match finding is exercised by every compression round trip of the other tests.
gtest:Snappy.FindMatchLengthRandom: Tests snappy::internal::FindMatchLength, a C++ helper of snappy-internal.h that is not part of the Rust API (see Snappy.FindMatchLength).

gtest:StubsGetFlagCharacterization.ReturnsArgument: snappy::GetFlag is a C++ template that stubs absl::GetFlag by returning its argument; flags are plain Rust values, so there is no Rust counterpart to test.
ctest:codecoremorph_characterization: only runs a GoogleTest binary, whose cases are mapped one by one
deviations: snappy::Sink: Abstract C++ interface, kept in C++ because other C++ code subclasses it; Rust holds its default behavior as free functions.
snappy::Sink::Sink: Empty constructor; stays in C++.
snappy::Sink::Append: Pure virtual; implemented by C++ subclasses.
snappy::Source: Abstract C++ interface, kept in C++ because other C++ code subclasses it.
snappy::Source::Source: Empty constructor; stays in C++.
snappy::Source::Available: Pure virtual; implemented by C++ subclasses (ByteArraySource::Available is ported).
snappy::Source::Peek: Pure virtual; implemented by C++ subclasses (ByteArraySource::Peek is ported).
snappy::Source::Skip: Pure virtual; implemented by C++ subclasses (ByteArraySource::Skip is ported).
snappy::ByteArraySource::ByteArraySource: The C++ constructor stores the pointer and length; Rust keeps only the length and a cursor offset.
snappy::ByteArraySource::Skip: Like the C++, skipping more than is left is not checked: the counts wrap.
snappy::UncheckedByteArraySink: The destination pointer is a C++ member; Rust holds the write logic as free functions.
snappy::UncheckedByteArraySink::UncheckedByteArraySink: Stores the destination pointer; stays in C++.
snappy::UncheckedByteArraySink::CurrentDestination: Simple accessor of the C++ destination pointer; stays in C++.
snappy::GetFlag: Stub of absl::GetFlag: a template that returns its argument; stays in C++.
snappy::STLStringResizeUninitialized: One call to std::string::resize; stays in C++.
snappy::LittleEndian: Static helper class; its functions are ported to free functions.
snappy::LittleEndian::IsLittleEndian: No longer constexpr; the Rust side decides from the target's endianness.
snappy::Bits: Static helper class; its functions are ported to free functions.
snappy::Bits::Log2FloorNonZero: The C++ assert(n != 0) is a debug_assert! in Rust.
snappy::Bits::FindLSBSetNonZero: The C++ assert(n != 0) is a debug_assert! in Rust.
snappy::Bits::FindLSBSetNonZero64: The C++ assert(n != 0) is a debug_assert! in Rust.
snappy::Varint: Static helper class; its functions are ported to free functions.

snappy::Compress: The Source/Sink overload is snappy::compress; the std::string overload is compress_to_vec. The Sink's GetAppendBuffer is no longer called: Rust compresses to its own buffer and appends it.
snappy::Uncompress: The std::string overload no longer checks the length against std::string::max_size().
snappy_status: The C enum is the #[repr(C)] enum snappy_status of the bridge; Status holds the two failures and success is Ok.
gtest:CorruptedTest.VerifyCorrupted: The pages guarding the ends of the buffers (mmap/mprotect) are gone: Rust slices are bounds checked.
gtest:Snappy.AppendSelfPatternExtensionEdgeCasesExhaustive: The random bytes come from a small generator of the test, not from std::mt19937.
gtest:Snappy.MaxBlowup: The random bytes come from a small generator of the test, not from std::mt19937.
gtest:Snappy.RandomData: The random inputs come from a small generator of the test, not from the C++ distributions, so they differ from the C++ run.
gtest:Snappy.ReadPastEndOfBuffer: The unreadable guard page after the buffer is gone: Rust slices are bounds checked.

gtest:Snappy.VerifyCharTable: The C++ test compares a computed table with the decompressor's lookup table char_table. The Rust decompressor has no such table, so the test checks the computed table against how the decompressor reads each of the 256 tags.

gtest:SnappyCApiTwoCharacterization.BufferTooSmall: The C++ test checked that the in/out length argument of the C function stays unchanged on failure; the Rust API has no such argument, so the test checks that the output buffer stays untouched.

gtest:SnappyCApiTwoCharacterization.InvalidInput: The C++ test checked that the in/out length argument of the C function stays unchanged on failure; the Rust API has no such argument, so the test checks that the output buffer stays untouched.
gtest:WorkingMemoryCharacterization.ScratchLayoutSmallInput: The Rust API describes the working memory as a layout of offsets (working_memory_layout) instead of pointers.

gtest:WorkingMemoryCharacterization.HashTableIsClearedOnEachRequest: The Rust API clears a caller-owned table (clear_hash_table); the C++ test also checked that the same table pointer comes back, which has no counterpart.
gtest:SinkSourceViaCApiCharacterization.SinkAndSourceBasics: The Rust functions work on offsets and slices instead of pointers.

gtest:SnappyCCharacterization.CompressBufferTooSmall: The C++ test checked that the in/out length argument stays unchanged on failure; the Rust API has no such argument, so the test checks that the output buffer stays untouched.
gtest:SnappyCCharacterization.UncompressBufferTooSmallLeavesLengthUntouched: The Rust API has no in/out length argument; the test checks that the output buffer stays untouched instead.

gtest:SnappyCCharacterization.InvalidInput: The C++ test checked that the in/out length argument stays unchanged on failure; the Rust API has no such argument, so the test checks that the output buffer stays untouched.
gtest:SinkCharacterization.DefaultGetAppendBufferReturnsScratch: The Rust function returns the offset into the scratch buffer (0) instead of a pointer.
gtest:SinkCharacterization.DefaultGetAppendBufferVariableReturnsScratch: The Rust function returns the offset into the scratch buffer (0) instead of a pointer.

gtest:SinkCharacterization.DefaultAppendAndTakeOwnershipAppendsAndCallsDeleter: The deleter is a closure without arguments; the C++ checks of the pointer and size passed to it are replaced by checks of the order of the calls.
gtest:ByteArraySourceCharacterization.AvailablePeekSkip: Peek returns an offset and a length instead of a pointer and a length.
gtest:ByteArraySourceCharacterization.EmptySourceAndZeroSkip: Peek returns an offset and a length instead of a pointer and a length.
gtest:UncheckedByteArraySinkCharacterization.AppendCopiesAndAdvances: The Rust functions return how far the destination moves instead of the destination pointer.
gtest:UncheckedByteArraySinkCharacterization.GetAppendBufferReturnsDestination: The Rust functions return offsets from the destination instead of pointers.
gtest:UncheckedByteArraySinkCharacterization.GetAppendBufferVariableUsesHint: The Rust function returns only the allocated size; the buffer is the destination itself.

gtest:UncheckedByteArraySinkCharacterization.AppendAndTakeOwnershipCopiesAndCallsDeleter: The deleter is a closure without arguments; the C++ checks of the pointer and size passed to it are replaced by checks that the source bytes are unchanged and the byte after the copy is untouched.
gtest:StubsUnalignedCharacterization.LoadsReadHostOrder: The Rust functions take the bytes as arrays (there are no unaligned pointers); only the 16 and 32 bit loads were tested in C++.
gtest:StubsUnalignedCharacterization.StoresWriteHostOrder: The Rust functions return the bytes to store; the test copies them into the buffer at the same offsets the C++ test wrote to.
gtest:LittleEndianCharacterization.Store16: The Rust function returns the bytes to store; the test copies them into the buffer at the same offsets the C++ test wrote to.
gtest:LittleEndianCharacterization.Store32: The Rust function returns the bytes to store; the test copies them into the buffer at the same offsets the C++ test wrote to.
gtest:LittleEndianCharacterization.Store64: The Rust function returns the bytes to store; the test copies them into the buffer at the same offsets the C++ test wrote to.

The run ended with status **completed**: all 12 units are committed and the final clean build and full test run passed. That was 75 tests, against a baseline of 62 passing.

The work is on branch `codecoremorph/20261105-120253-a596` (last commit `4d86d4e2e5df`), which took about 46 minutes. Your working tree and `main` are untouched.

## What was done

- **Characterization tests:** snappy had untested code, so I first wrote 41 C++ tests in 5 jobs (C-0001 to C-0005) to pin its current behaviour. All were accepted.
- **Plan:** I approved the full 12-unit plan without exclusions.
- **Module ports (U-0001 to U-0004):** each C++ module's logic now lives in the Rust crate `snappy_rs`, with thin C++ facades that forward through a bridge.
  - U-0001 is `snappy-sinksource` and U-0002 is `snappy-stubs-internal`.
  - U-0003 is `snappy.cc`, the compressor and decompressor.
  - U-0004 is `snappy-c`. Its five C functions are now exported straight from Rust, and `snappy-c.cc` only includes the header.
- **Executable (U-0005):** `snappy_test_tool` is now a Rust binary and its C++ source is deleted.
- **Test translations (U-0006 to U-0011):** the 20 cases in `snappy_unittest.cc` and the 5 characterization files are now Rust tests, with a test map pairing each C++ test to its Rust one.
- **Retirement (U-0012):** the codemod deleted the C++ and the CMake build on its own, with no edits from me.

## What the verification did not cover

- **Tests with no Rust counterpart:**
  - `Snappy.FindMatchLength` and `Snappy.FindMatchLengthRandom` test a C++-only helper that isn't in the Rust API. The report flags that the translations check less than the originals.
  - `StubsGetFlagCharacterization.ReturnsArgument` tests a C++ stub (`absl::GetFlag`) and maps to nothing.
  - The two CTest entries that only launch a GoogleTest binary are mapped to nothing as well.
- **Parity warnings:** the report flags two units, U-0007 and U-0010. In U-0007 the translated test makes 3 checks where the original made 4; the missing one compared a returned pointer. U-0010 is the `GetFlag` case above. I approved both units because each gap has no Rust equivalent.
- **Other test differences:**
  - The C++ checks that an in/out length argument stays unchanged on failure now check the buffer is untouched instead.
  - Several pointer checks became offset checks.
  - The random tests use a small generator of their own, so their inputs differ from the C++ run.
  - The guard-page tests are gone because Rust slices are bounds-checked.
- **Behaviour changes:**
  - `Compress` no longer calls the sink's `GetAppendBuffer`.
  - The SSSE3/BMI2/branchless fast paths are gone, so speed differs, and the functions that used to be inline in `snappy-stubs-internal.h` are now calls through the bridge.
  - The string overloads no longer check `std::string::max_size()`.
  - `snappy_test_tool` no longer measures zlib, LZO or LZ4; it logs "library not compiled in" on stderr.
  - An empty input file now measures one empty block instead of hitting the C++ undefined behaviour.
- **Unverified file:** the build doesn't compile `rust/snappy_rs/include/snappy_rs/bridge.hpp`, so its changes in U-0002 are unverified.
- **Unsafe code:** none outside the bridge.

## Review

Run `git diff 2b63814 codecoremorph/20261105-120253-a596` or `git log` on that branch. Merging is up to you. The full report is at `E:\codecoremorph-home\bench\snappy\.codecoremorph\runs\20261105-120253-a596\report.md`.
